limitations: Initial artifact SHA256 60a561... only; final rebuild and installation must be validated separately.
The initial permission flow required a retry after a denial result and was subsequently changed. This initial run does not validate that subsequent permission fix.
The native Linux viewer and browser probe were simultaneous legitimate receivers during part of this run. This is a two-peer workload, not a single-peer benchmark.
Decoded cadence is computed as delta framesDecoded / delta inbound-rtp RTCStats.timestamp in milliseconds. Intervals spanning camera/settings/generation changes are excluded from cadence metrics.
Sampling approximately every five seconds demonstrates observed counter progress and connection state; it cannot rule out every shorter pause between samples.
These metrics do not measure end-to-end latency, battery cost, sustained 60 FPS support or a performance improvement against a controlled baseline.

Configured FPS and resolution are ceilings/settings. Negotiated sizes and actual FPS can adapt with hardware, lighting and receiver load. The work changes camera UI and lifecycle presentation; FPS values are not presented as an improvement claim.
Browser H264 codec identity is directly present in these new samples, even though an older generic helper still says codec identity is unavailable.
Initial PC Stop and reconnect are not approved: the Stop click missed after the window resized, and the native log contains one viewer connection before exit code 0.
USB cable and iOS device behavior were not physically tested in this run.

limits: Physical validation used one S22 Ultra and one Linux PC over Wi-Fi; other Android devices and iOS are not physically verified.
